title: Gully's key
logline: Tuesday. After hours at the shuttered frame shop, with Gully's key. Gully has a key because he fixes the furnace. Wood cuts a mat for the invitation on the old cutter. 'Pull, don't push.' He hears her say it.

panels.composition: The frame shop, dark, three years closed. GULLY at the door with a key. WOOD with the cream card in an envelope.

characters.pose: at the door with a key

balloons.text: Why do you have a key.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink, a stocky man unlocking a dark shuttered frame shop's door while a thin man waits holding a cream envelope

panels.composition: Inside. Dust. The mat cutter under a sheet. Wood pulling the sheet off. The cutter as it was.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink, a thin man pulling a dust sheet off a mat cutter in a dark closed shop

panels.composition: The blade. His hands. The cut. Pull, don't push. The strip letters her line in a small balloon with no tail, from nowhere.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink, close-up of a man's hands making a bevel cut on a mat cutter with a small tailless speech balloon floating nearby
image.notes: The owner's line, from nowhere. She's not in the shop. A balloon with no tail.

panels.composition: The mat, cut. Cream on cream. Gully holding the flashlight. Wood holding the mat to the flashlight like a window.

characters.pose: holding the mat to the light

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink, a thin man holding a cut mat up to a flashlight held by a stocky man in a dark shop

art.line: razor-sharp, confident brush and ink; pristine perspective; crisp silhouettes; zero crosshatch in close-ups
art.palette: dailies: black ink, one spot tone at most. Sundays: wet-on-wet — gray-green moss, fog, rusted tin, bruised dusk
art.paper: bristol for dailies; 140 lb Arches cold-press for Sundays

notes: 'Furnace doesn't know that.' Her line, from nowhere.
